AdapterRun.description: One adapter's contribution to a corpus: which adapter, and the range it read.

budget.description:
The diff budget report of the evidence the corpus was authored from. Set
on the run of the `DIFFS` adapter.

from.description:
The full hash of the range's base commit: the commit the previous release
was tagged on. Absent for a release line with no release yet, whose range
starts at its root.

to.description:
The full hash of the range's head commit: the newest commit the adapter
read.

BudgetReport.description: How much patch text a bundle carries against its limit.

omitted.description: The patches the budget left out or cut.

total.description: Bytes of patch text before the budget applied.

Bump.description: The release impact of a change or of a release as a whole.

CommitEvidence.description: Everything the bundle holds about one commit.

conventional.description: The parsed conventional subject, where the subject is one.

diff.description: The commit's diff. Absent WHEN the Diff Collector did not run.

pull_request.description: The pull request the commit carries, where it carries one.

record.description: The commit record: hash, subject, body, trailers, author and files.

signal.description: The classifier's reading of the commit. Absent when unclassified.

CommitRecord.description:
The records the collectors produce.

Collection is deliberately free of interpretation: these records carry what
git and the hosting platform said, parsed into fields but not given meaning.
Deciding what a trailer means, or which records become changelog entries, is
the business of the components that consume them.

author_date.description: The author date, RFC 3339, as `git log --format=%aI` prints it.

author_email.description: The commit author's email address, as git recorded it.

author_name.description: The commit author's name, as git recorded it.

body.description:
The commit body — everything after the subject.

Where a repository squashes using the pull request description, this is
that description, which is how pull request prose reaches the release
without the hosting platform being consulted.

conventional.description:
The parsed conventional-commit subject, where the subject is one.

Absent for a subject that does not follow the convention.

pull_request.description:
The pull request the commit carries, where it carries one.

Absent for a commit pushed directly to a release line.

subject.description:
The commit subject — its first line.

For a squash merge this is the pull request title, with the pull request
reference the hosting platform appends still present.

trailers.description:
Trailers parsed from the body as key-value pairs.

Recorded without interpretation. A release-type trailer means something
to the bump classifier and nothing here.

Conventional.description: The parts of a conventional-commit subject.

breaking.description:
Whether the subject carries a `!` marker or the body a `BREAKING CHANGE:`
footer.

scope.description: The scope, where the subject names one.

type.description: The type as written, for example `feat`.

DiffRecord.description: The changes one commit made, as patch text.

commit.description: The commit the diff is of.

truncated.description: Whether the budget cut some patch text.

Evidence.description:
The evidence a producer authors a release's changelog from.

The tooling builds an Evidence instance and a producer reads it; a producer
never builds one. It states what git said without interpreting it.

base_version.description:
The version the range starts from, without a tag prefix. Absent for a
release line with no release yet.

budget.description: How much patch text the bundle carries against its limit.

commits.description: The commits in the range, oldest first.

purpose.description: What the bundle is evidence for.

range.description: The commit range the bundle covers.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema that the instance conforms to.

sources.description: The adapters that contributed material to the bundle.

EvidencePurpose.description: What a bundle is evidence for.

previous_path.description: The path before the change. Set for a rename or copy.

status.description: How the commit changed the file.

patch.description: The unified diff text for this file.

truncated.description: Whether the budget cut this patch.

FileStatus.description: How a commit changed a file.

OmissionReason.description: Why a patch is not carried whole.

OmittedDiff.description: A patch the bundle left out or cut.

commit.description: The commit the patch belongs to.

path.description: The file the patch is of.

reason.description: Why the patch is not carried whole.

truncated.description: Whether part of the patch was carried.

PullRequestInfo.description: The pull request a commit carries.

description.description: The pull request description, where known.

origin.description: Where the number, title and description were read from.

title.description: The pull request title, where known.

PullRequestOrigin.description: Where a pull request's information was read from.

Range.description: The commit range a bundle covers.

from.description:
The full hash of the base commit. Absent for a release line with no
release yet, whose range starts at its root.

to.description: The full hash of the head commit.
